applies_why: The judge text weighs a collision between the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain on footing, which is the situation Rule K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse
room: 'footing': I weighed reading it as whether each chain has a sound foundation in the verses beneath it, versus reading it as whether the chain's own links are explicitly stated; I took footing to mean the former, which the judge uses.
why: The judge compares the two chains by their footing and does not weigh any single verse against the other, which is what Rule K-C requires.
